title: Prime spectra and principal localizations of a ring fibre product
statement:
Let $A,D,E$ be commutative rings with identity, let $\alpha:A\twoheadrightarrow D$ be a surjective ring homomorphism and $\beta:E\to D$ any ring homomorphism. Put $B=A\times_D E=\{(a,e):\alpha(a)=\beta(e)\}$, with coordinatewise operations. Write $p:B\to A$, $q:B\to E$ for the projections. The map induced by the spectra of $p$ and $q$ is a homeomorphism
$$\bigl(|\operatorname{Spec}A|\amalg|\operatorname{Spec}E|\bigr)/\!\sim\ \xrightarrow{\sim}|\operatorname{Spec}B|,$$
where the quotient has the quotient topology and $\sim$ is generated by identifying the two images of each point of $\operatorname{Spec}D$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. For every $h=(a,e)\in B$, put $d=\alpha(a)=\beta(e)$. The natural ring map is an isomorphism
$$B_h\xrightarrow{\sim} A_a\times_{D_d}E_e,$$
where $R_r$ means the ring localization at the powers of $r$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away]; the isomorphisms commute with further principal localizations. Zero rings and zero elements $h$ are allowed.

proof.text: Let $Q$ be the quotient space in the statement, and $j_A,j_E$ its two structure maps. A pair of continuous maps from the two spectra descends to a continuous map from $Q$ exactly when it agrees on $\operatorname{Spec}D$: being constant on the generating identifications is equivalent to being constant on their generated equivalence relation, and continuity follows from the quotient topology. Apply [lem-sfb-fibre-product-spectrum-topology] with $T=E$ and $P=B$. Its hypotheses are precisely the given surjectivity of $\alpha$ and the arbitrary map $\beta$. Its universal property gives a continuous map $\operatorname{Spec}B\to Q$ restricting to $j_A,j_E$. Conversely, the two projection-induced maps to $\operatorname{Spec}B$ agree on $\operatorname{Spec}D$, hence descend to a continuous map $Q\to\operatorname{Spec}B$. Both composites restrict to identity maps on the two spectra. The structure maps into $Q$ are jointly surjective by construction, and those into $\operatorname{Spec}B$ are jointly surjective by the cited node, so both composites are identities. This is the asserted homeomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0B7J, lemma-points-of-fibre-product, statement and first paragraph of proof; quotient-space universal property written out.

proof.text: Fix $h=(a,e)$ and $d=\alpha(a)=\beta(e)$. Define $\Phi_h:B_h\to A_a\times_{D_d}E_e$ by $\Phi_h((x,y)/h^n)=(x/a^n,y/e^n)$. The pair has equal images in $D_d$ because $\alpha(x)=\beta(y)$. If two fractions of $B_h$ are equal, the equality criterion in [def-weil-ring-localization-away], projected to $A$ and $E$, says that both coordinate fractions are equal. Thus the formula is well defined. The fraction formulas for addition, multiplication and the unit show coordinatewise that it is a unital ring homomorphism. For example, addition of numerators $h^m(x,y)+h^n(x\prime,y\prime)$ over $h^{n+m}$ gives exactly the coordinatewise sums. It extends the two projections, and therefore is the natural map in the statement.

source.place: Tag 01Z8, lemma-diagram-localize; explicit fraction verification of the localized cartesian square.

proof.text: If $\Phi_h((x,y)/h^n)=0$, the zero criterion of [def-weil-ring-localization-away] gives integers $r,s\geq0$ with $a^rx=0$ and $e^sy=0$. Put $k=\max(r,s)$. Then $h^k(x,y)=(0,0)$, so $(x,y)/h^n=0$ by the same criterion. Since $\Phi_h$ is additive, applying this to the difference of any two elements with the same image proves injectivity.

source.place: Tag 01Z8, lemma-diagram-localize; explicit fraction verification of the localized cartesian square.

proof.text: Given a pair $(x/a^r,y/e^s)$ in the fibre product, put $N=\max(r,s)$, $X=a^{N-r}x$ and $Y=e^{N-s}y$. Its two images in $D_d$ are $\alpha(X)/d^N$ and $\beta(Y)/d^N$. Equality of these fractions, by [def-weil-ring-localization-away], implies $d^{k+N}(\alpha(X)-\beta(Y))=0$ for some $k\geq0$. Set $L=k+N$. Then $\alpha(a^LX)=\beta(e^LY)$, so $b=(a^LX,e^LY)$ belongs to $B$. The fraction $b/h^{N+L}$ maps to $(X/a^N,Y/e^N)=(x/a^r,y/e^s)$. This proves surjectivity; together with the preceding step it proves that $\Phi_h$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 01Z8, lemma-diagram-localize; explicit fraction verification of the localized cartesian square.

proof.text: For a further element $t=(c,f)\in B$ and $b=(x,y)\in B$, either order of applying the comparison and localizing sends $b/(h^nt^m)$ to $(x/(a^nc^m),y/(e^nf^m))$, with common image in the iterated localization of $D$. These fractions represent every element of the iterated localization by [def-weil-ring-localization-away], so the two ring maps agree. This also covers further localization at any element $t/h^r\in B_h$: since $h$ is already a unit, inverting $t/h^r$ is equivalent to inverting $t$, and the same coordinate formulas apply. No step cancelled a power or assumed a nonzero ring or element. If $h=0$, the zero criterion makes $B_h,A_a,E_e,D_d$ zero rings. If $D=0$, the formula reduces to localization of $A\times E$, with the same common-denominator proof. Thus the allowed degenerate cases are included.

lean.statement: theorem ringFibreProduct_spectrum_localization {A D E : CommRingCat.{u}} (α : A ⟶ D) (β : E ⟶ D) (hα : Function.Surjective α.hom) : (∃ e : Quot (fibreProductSpectrumRelation α β) ≃ₜ PrimeSpectrum (pullbackCone α β).pt, (∀ x : PrimeSpectrum A, e (Quot.mk _ (Sum.inl x)) = PrimeSpectrum.comap (pullbackCone α β).fst.hom x) ∧ (∀ x : PrimeSpectrum E, e (Quot.mk _ (Sum.inr x)) = PrimeSpectrum.comap (pullbackCone α β).snd.hom x)) ∧ (∃ e : ∀ h : (pullbackCone α β).pt, Localization.Away h ≃+* (principalFibreProduct α β h).pt, (∀ h : (pullbackCone α β).pt, (principalFibreProduct α β h).fst.hom.comp (e h).toRingHom = Localization.awayMap (pullbackCone α β).fst.hom h ∧ (principalFibreProduct α β h).snd.hom.comp (e h).toRingHom = Localization.awayMap (pullbackCone α β).snd.hom h) ∧ ∀ (h : (pullbackCone α β).pt) (z : Localization.Away h), ∃ ez : Localization.Away z ≃+* (principalFibreProduct (ofHom (Localization.awayMap α.hom h.val.1)) (ofHom (awayMapTo β.hom h.val.2 (α.hom h.val.1) h.property.symm)) (e h z)).pt, (principalFibreProduct (ofHom (Localization.awayMap α.hom h.val.1)) (ofHom (awayMapTo β.hom h.val.2 (α.hom h.val.1) h.property.symm)) (e h z)).fst.hom.comp ez.toRingHom = Localization.awayMap ((principalFibreProduct α β h).fst.hom.comp (e h).toRingHom) z ∧ (principalFibreProduct (ofHom (Localization.awayMap α.hom h.val.1)) (ofHom (awayMapTo β.hom h.val.2 (α.hom h.val.1) h.property.symm)) (e h z)).snd.hom.comp ez.toRingHom = Localization.awayMap ((principalFibreProduct α β h).snd.hom.comp (e h).toRingHom) z)
